subject: DPA Annex: Residency Matrix, Access Roles, and Transfer Risk Log
messages:
From: Maria Torres <maria.torres@healthsync.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA Annex — initial residency & access questions

Hi Aisha & Grace,

Thanks for sending over the draft DPA annex earlier. Procurement asked me to double-check a couple of items that are critical for our internal security review before we can advance to signature:

- Can you provide a concise residency matrix that maps each data class (PHI, PII, telemetry, aggregated analytics) to the processing locations (hosted region, dedicated, private) and any default cross-border transfer behavior?
- For role-based access, we need a diagram or a short table that shows which Redwood roles (Support, Ops, SRE, ModelOps, Legal) can access raw PII, encrypted blobs, and tokenized identifiers.
- Please confirm KMS key custody model and whether HealthSync can require a customer-managed key for our dedicated/private deployments.

We have an internal deadline of next Wednesday; attached is a redline of the DPA with a few line comments. Also CC'ing Tim from procurement (tim.cho@healthsync.com).

Thanks,
Maria Torres
Head of Privacy & Compliance
HealthSync
Attachments: healthsync_dpa_annex_v2_redline.docx (docx)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Torres <maria.torres@healthsync.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Tim Cho <tim.cho@healthsync.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA Annex — initial residency & access questions

Hi Maria (and Tim),

Appreciate the quick review. See attached a compact residency_matrix_2027-03.csv and a small access_role_map_v2.png that summarizes the internal access boundaries we enforce by default. A few key notes inline below — I'll leave technical confirmations to Jordan for the KMS specifics.

Summary answers (high level):
- Residency: Hosted API processes in region selected by the tenant (we publish region locations). Dedicated is customer-isolated; Private deployments run in-customer environment and do not cross customer boundaries. For hosted we offer configuration to pin storage and inference to a region; otherwise short-term KV caching may replicate within the same continent for performance.
- Access roles: Support and basic CS roles can see metadata and anonymized request logs only. Ops/SRE have access to metrics and runtime traces; ModelOps and Engineering never have default access to persisted raw PII unless scoped by an explicit least-privilege request and logged justification.
- KMS: We support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers may opt into CMK for persistent storage; ephemeral in-memory caches are encrypted with server-side keys. Jordan — can you confirm export restrictions and if we provide an HSM-backed attestation report?

Action items:
1) Jordan to attach KMS attestation and confirm exportability conditions (by EOD Thu).
2) I will update the DPA annex to reflect the residency matrix and role mappings where appropriate and re-upload by Friday.
3) If HealthSync needs additional contractual language around no-cross-border by default, we can draft a narrow clause for procurement to review.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0192
Attachments: residency_matrix_2027-03.csv (csv), access_role_map_v2.png (image)

From: Maria Torres <maria.torres@healthsync.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Cho <tim.cho@healthsync.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA Annex — initial residency & access questions

Thanks Aisha — that reads much better. A few follow-ups after reviewing the attachments:

- The residency matrix is helpful but procurement wants a column that shows whether each processing activity (inference, embeddings, logging, audit exports) can be prevented from leaving the customer-designated region under default settings. Can you add that?
- On access roles: we need stronger guarantees on emergency access. Specifically, what is the process and approval chain for Break-Glass access? Who signs the justification, who gets notified, and how long is the access window?
- KMS attestations: we need either an HSM-backed attestation or a SOC-like evidence bundle that demonstrates key separation. If Jordan can provide a short attestation template or pointer to an existing artifact, that will satisfy our legal/security reviewers.

Also — procurement asked for an estimate of time for making the small DPA language change and whether Redwood will accept a limited addendum for 'no cross-border data transfer' for Hosted API by region. Tim and I prefer a simple two-paragraph addendum if possible.

Regards,
Maria

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Torres <maria.torres@healthsync.com>, Tim Cho <tim.cho@healthsync.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA Annex — residency & access questions (summary & next steps)

Hi Maria / Tim — Jordan from Privacy Ops here. Thanks for the clear asks; below is a concise delivery plan and answers to your bullets.

Break-glass / emergency access:
- Process: request submitted to our incident approvals queue -> approval by on-call privacy lead + engineering manager -> access window auto-revoked after 4 hours unless extended with explicit new approval. All events logged and sent to the customer's audit webhook if configured.
- Notifications: primary contact (customer-designated) + internal audit team; justification must include ticket link and affected resource IDs.

KMS / attestation:
- We can provide an HSM-backed attestation for Dedicated & Private: standard exportable attestation PDF (includes HSM vendor, certs, and access control summary). For Hosted, we provide a SOC-style artifact plus optional CMK for persistent stores. Attached is a redwood_kms_attestation_stub.pdf (placeholder) and the updated residency matrix with a "prevent_cross_border_by_default" column included.

Contract language & timeline:
- We can accept a short addendum for "region-bound processing" on Hosted for customers who opt-in; Redwood will need a scoped paragraph and a technical runbook to operationalize. Drafting a two-paragraph addendum should take our legal team 2 business days after we agree on the technical constraints.
- Deliverables and ETA:
  1) Updated DPA annex with residency column and Break-Glass clause: by Fri, 2027-03-05 EOD (Aisha).
  2) KMS attestation artifact: draft by Thu, 2027-03-04 EOD (Jordan) — final within 3 business days pending internal review.

Next steps: Aisha will upload the updated annex and I will attach the attestation. If that looks good, Tim / procurement can circulate the two-paragraph addendum for signature.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Privacy Operations, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0147
